reason: Reviewed lifecycle-hook guidance, the Notifai skill and its references, harness setup, CLI readiness, and domain/trust terms against Claude Code command approval. Outside a mode that skips permission prompts, Claude Code asks at the terminal before each Bash command it has no rule for, so an away User's question, its wake-up and its acknowledgement could each wait for an approval nobody sees. Setup now offers one explicit, User-owned choice once Claude Code is wired: init --claude-commands adds allow rules for send, ask, receive, acknowledge, status, replies, close, guidance and session rename to the User's Claude Code settings, and --no-claude-commands declines. Readiness reports the state as claude-commands and never blocks on it. An unattended run without the flag changes nothing. Setup, configuration, guidance edits, logs and sign-out keep their prompt, and hooks uninstall removes the rules with the wiring. The harness setup reference and README now describe the choice, say it is the User's grant, and tell agents never to add the rules unasked or edit Claude Code permission settings by hand. The skill itself is unchanged: it already directs agents to that reference for installation and keeps every setup decision with the User.
